label: Tier D repair — the two convertible with existing engines (lineRelationLab, dilationExplore)

widget.prompt: You have measured the corresponding angles and found them equal. Turn the blue line until its angle matches the dark line's — and watch whether that alone is enough to force them parallel.
widget.successFeedback: Equal angles, and the lines are parallel — that is the CONVERSE doing the work, not the original theorem. The forward theorem starts from parallel and hands you equal angles; here you started from equal angles and got parallel. Same two facts, opposite arrows, and only the converse licenses this direction.
widget.angleFeedback: The angles still differ, so the lines still converge somewhere. Match the angle exactly — the converse needs EQUAL corresponding angles, not merely close ones.
widget.distanceFeedback: The direction is right. Sliding the line changes where it sits but never whether it is parallel — position is not what the converse is about.

widget.prompt: Land the shape exactly on its target using a rigid motion — translate, and reflect if you need to. Watch the side lengths and the corner angles the whole way.
widget.successFeedback: It lands exactly, and nothing about the shape itself ever changed: every side kept its length and every corner kept its angle. That is what 'rigid' means — BOTH distances and angle measures survive, which is why congruent figures match part-for-part for free.
widget.offsetFeedback: Not on the target yet. Translation slides the shape without altering a single length or angle — keep moving it.
widget.reflectFeedback: A reflection flips the shape across the axis. Like translation it is rigid: the mirror image has identical side lengths and identical angles, just a reversed orientation.

refusals.title: Degree & Like Terms
refusals.why: Searched the full manip>=2 catalogue for a polynomial-TERM engine and found none — no z.literal matching polynomial/term/degree/coefficient exists in schema.ts. algebraTiles was the nearest candidate and was checked directly: its only targets are targetX and targetConst, i.e. a LINEAR ax + b tiling, so it cannot represent 3x² + 5x⁴ − x at all, let alone its degree. Every question in this lesson (degree, leading coefficient, constant term, which pair are like terms) reads a symbolic expression's NOTATION rather than manipulating a quantity. Refused — a genuine engine gap, not a fit failure.

refusals.title: Rotations as Functions, Rotational Symmetry
refusals.why: DEFERRED, NOT REFUSED — pending an engine decision. Both lessons are entirely about ROTATION: coordinate rules ((x,y)→(−y,x) etc.), composing turns by adding angles, and rotational symmetry order. transformExplore's full schema was read directly and has shape/target/gridMin/gridMax/dxMin/dxMax/dyMin/dyMax/allowReflect — translation and reflection only, NO rotation field of any kind. dilationExplore scales from a centre but does not turn. This is the rotation-engine gap flagged since S203S as a build candidate; these two lessons are the concrete case for it, and both would convert immediately if a rotation-capable engine existed. Recorded as deferred so the fit rate is not charged for an engine that has not been built.
